feedback: The candidate is a single, bounded step from the iteration 1 design (score 97.7331, the best raced so far). It lowers base_speed from 1.4 to 1.2, lowers kp from 3.5 to 3.0, and keeps kd 0.3, ki 0.1, sensor_size 0.016 and the geometry unchanged. The change follows the rules in the iteration 1 feedback. Iteration 1 showed line_loss_events of 1.0 in all 60 trials and max_error of 0.062 to 0.064, just past the 0.06 m limit, so the base_speed cut is the right first lever. It also showed steering_oscillation of 0.24 on the oval and 0.21 on the s-bend, above the 0.2 level, so the kp reduction is also justified. The candidate is valid: all sensor positions are in range, sensor_size 0.016 is allowed, and the controller values are inside their limits. Nothing is obviously broken. Its main risk is that base_speed 1.2 may be too slow to finish within 3 s, which needs roughly 1.5 m/s, so completion is unlikely at this setting. Progress is the score lever for now. I cannot say how it will perform. This is early exploration with 9 iterations left, so racing it gives the telemetry the next critique needs. Next race, read the results as follows. If line_loss_events is still 1.0 with max_error above 0.06, the cause is probably geometry. The 5-sensor span of 0.08 m means the robot leaves the sensed area at about 0.06 m offset, so widen the sensor span or change sensor spacing next. If the run is clean (line_loss_events near 0, steering_oscillation under 0.2) but completion_time is above 3 s, raise base_speed in steps of 0.1 while keeping kp near 3.0. If steering_oscillation is still above 0.2 at kp 3.0, raise kd or lower kp further before changing speed.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is still 1.0 and max_error is above 0.06 on the oval or s-bend, keep base_speed at 1.2 and widen the sensor span (for example x at ±0.06 m, or sensor_positions spaced 0.03 m). Iteration 1 showed line loss at 1.0 in every trial at base_speed 1.4 with kp 3.5, so speed alone may not fix it.

If the run is clean (line_loss_events near 0, steering_oscillation under 0.2) but completion_time is above 3 s, raise base_speed in 0.1 steps (for example 1.3, then 1.4) and keep kp at 3.0 and kd at 0.3. Iteration 1 at base_speed 1.4 gave progress of 0.37 on the oval, so the limit is not yet known.

If steering_oscillation is still above 0.2 with kp 3.0, raise kd from 0.3 toward 0.45 or lower kp toward 2.6, leaving base_speed unchanged. Iteration 1 had oscillation of 0.24 on the oval at kp 3.5 and kd 0.3.
